content.text:
The edit went through: `return 1` is now `return 2` in `app.py`. I made one Edit call, as you asked.

The exact tool result was:

> The file <LIVE>\U-1-Edit-1\repo\app.py has been updated successfully.

A PreToolUse hook also attached this warning to the call:

> Mneme availability: authorization could not be verified (AUTHORIZATION_UNVERIFIABLE, reason NETWORK). This edit proceeded without fail-closed availability enforcement.

So the hook couldn't reach its authorization check because of a network problem, and it let the edit through instead of blocking it. If the latest commit (ADR-033) was meant to make the protection fail closed, it did not fail closed here.
